summary_en: This Phase 2 study is testing Orca-T, an allogeneic stem cell and T-cell immunotherapy biologic, after reduced intensity or non-myeloablative conditioning. It is being studied in people with acute myeloid leukemia, mixed phenotype acute leukemia, or myelodysplastic syndromes who are undergoing allogeneic transplant. How Orca-T is given and how long or how often are not stated. The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, and efficacy, but the main outcome is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa Orca-T, un biológico de inmunoterapia con células madre y linfocitos T de donante alogénico, después de un acondicionamiento de intensidad reducida o no mieloablativo. Se estudia en personas con leucemia mieloide aguda, leucemia aguda de fenotipo mixto o síndromes mielodisplásicos que se someterán a un trasplante alogénico. No se indica cómo se administra Orca-T ni la duración o frecuencia. El estudio evaluará la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la eficacia, pero el resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Acute myeloid or mixed phenotype leukemia in complete remission or CR with incomplete hematologic recovery.
Myelodysplastic syndrome indicated for transplant, with 10% or less blasts in the bone marrow.
Planned reduced intensity or non-myeloablative transplant, with an 8/8 HLA-matched related or unrelated donor.
Meets stated organ function limits and is judged not eligible for a fully myeloablative transplant by the principal investigator.
not_for: Current immunosuppressive therapy, or corticosteroids above 10 mg/day (topical and low-dose oral exceptions).
Planned donor lymphocyte infusion or planned T-cell depletion.
Uncontrolled infection, or positive HIV, HTLV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C test, with exceptions.
